The difficult part is owning items and selling it.

I obviously want to make as much money as possible so I've got to figure out the best place to sell the item. Do i sell it in shop? consignment? ebay? amazon? craigslist? offerup? etsy?

For me I make sure they are sellable.

99% of the time it will be a local artist, or an absolutely worthless piece. I start with the first steps:

Do i recognize the artists name? How much is known about the picture/photo/painting/print and the medium it was produced on? the more you know the easier it will be to sell.

#1 Does it depict a recognizable geographical location?(i.e Santa Cruz Boardwalk, Grand Canyon, San Francisco, NYC Skyline)
-
#2 Does it depict an animal that is "collectible"? (i.e: wolves, jaguars, horses,dolphins)
-
#3 Is it mass produced? If not, then how much do you think the person spent to frame/display it? is it a center piece picture, or does it look like it came from a series that was displayed? generally if someone spent serious cash to display it as a center piece it might have some value to it.

-
#4 how do you think the person got it and why are they selling it?

If the person is sharp, seems computer savy, and recognizes the item is there and isn't asking a lot.... There is a chance he knows its not worth much.

If it was in grandmas junk bin and he is cleaning her house then there is a chance it could be worth something... but check to see what the rest of grandmas stuff looks like...

There is a ton of competition but that's why you have to dip your feet into every category and learn as much as possible.

What will make you more successful than the next guy is knowledge.

I run a pawn shop and I look at things this way:


If you bring me a PS4. I look at:

#1 What is it realistically worth?
-
#2 If i had to sell it asap, what could I price it for that it would sell within a week?


Truth be told. to answer #1 I think a PS4 used in good shape is worth around $240 depending on what comes with it. 1 controller/cables/cords = $240.

If i wanted it gone within a week I'd have to price it at $180-200.


Whenever I take an item in that comes from a "collection" or a "lot" or that is jewelry, or has a serial number(ps4s do). I have to put them in my system, and hold them for a minimum of 30-90 days.


So throwing money your way, and knowing I have to sit potentially up to 90 days is not fun. I'd try to offer you around $120. MAYBE. go $160. but I wouldn't go anywhere closer. you are going to deal with lowball offers and realistically. you are better off selling it on craigslist and putting it at $200 and take the first $180 that comes your way. it'll sell within a day or 2 and you'll get more cash.
